title: HANDLING MARITAL CONFLICTS
mv: Be ye angry, and sin not: let not the sun go down upon your wrath.
mvp: “Be ye angry, and sin not: let not the sun go down upon your wrath.”Ephesians 4:26
assignment: Identify five (5) biblical marriage or family conflicts (2x5=10 Marks).

b.x: Marital conflict is inevitable between two people with different personalities, backgrounds and expectations. However, this conflict does not have to destroy intimacy, peace, or trust. When handled with wisdom, conflict in marriage can strengthen the bond rather than weaken it. The goal should be to manage it without the painful fallout of bitterness, resentment, broken trust or broken marriage.
No marriage is immune to conflicts; even biblical couples faced challenges (Genesis 16:5-6). This understanding helps couples to approach conflicts with calmness.

Common causes of conflict include: miscommunication (Proverbs 18:21); unmet expectations and assumptions (Genesis 30:1); finance (1 Timothy 5:8); differences in parenting style (Proverbs 29:15); extended family interference, selfishness and pride (James 4:1-2), etc.
Some of the consequences of mishandled conflicts are emotional distance, loss of trust, bitterness, abuse, separation, negative impact on children and family instability, etc.
Here are some ways to manage conflicts and prevent negative fallout in marital relationships:

Choose love over ego. When conflicts arise, responding with patience rather than defensiveness can help de-escalate tensions and foster a more constructive conversation (Proverbs 15:1). It is, therefore, important to practice active listening (James 1:19). Hence, seek to understand your partner's view before trying to be understood. Maintain a constructive and respectful tone in conflicts, avoid personal attacks and focus on finding solutions (Proverbs 15:28). Refrain from blaming or finger-pointing. Avoid hurtful or derogatory language (Proverbs 15:2). Use the ‘We’ instead of ‘You’ language (Colossians 4:6), e.g., “We need to work on this” rather than “You always mess up.” This promotes teamwork instead of opposition. Learn to focus on the present issue, rather than bringing up past grievances. Know when to pause and take a break if emotions run too high (Ecclesiastes 3:7). Seek forgiveness and reconcile quickly (Ephesians 4:26) because forgiveness prevents resentment from taking root. Invite God into the process (Luke 18:1). Prayer softens the heart and helps couples see each other with grace (Matthew 18:19-20).
Conflict in marriage is not a curse but an opportunity. When handled in love, humility and wisdom, disagreements can become stepping stones to deeper intimacy.
